How to read a Ford part number: prefix, base and suffix

EKS LKW · 06.11.2026

Ford part numbers look hard to read, but they follow a fixed structure. Once you know it, you can quickly tell whether two numbers are the same part or just look alike.

The three parts

Take the clutch release bearing 3C46 7548 BA as an example:

3C46 — the prefix
Generally shows the design period and the vehicle programme. Cargo parts often carry prefixes such as 3C46, 9C46, AC46 or CC46.
7548 — the base
Tells you what kind of part it is. The same base number means the same function, whatever the prefix.
BA — the suffix
Marks the version or revision of the part. AA is usually the first version; AB, BA and so on are later changes.

The base shows the part group

Ford base numbers are grouped by system. Some groups you will see often in our catalogue:

  • 2xxx — brakes (e.g. 2L324, parking brake valve)
  • 3xxx — steering and front axle (3304, drag link)
  • 6xxx — engine
  • 7xxx — clutch and gearbox (7550 clutch disc, 7548 release bearing)
  • 8xxx — cooling
  • 9xxx — fuel and emissions

Every part page on FordCargo.ro states which group the base number belongs to.

Don't drop the suffix

Two parts with the same base and different suffixes may be interchangeable, but they may also differ: another length, another number of splines, another connector. Always search the full number. If you only have part of it, say so in your request so we can check the versions.

How to type it in the search

In the site search you can type the number with spaces, with hyphens or joined up: 3C46 7548 BA, 3C46-7548-BA and 3C467548BA find the same part. Watch out for 0 and O, 1 and I: the letters O and I are rare in Ford numbers, so it is usually a digit.

A catalogue result is a starting point. We confirm that it fits your truck in the quote.
